passages.text: Then Job answered: “Even today my complaint is bitter. His hand is heavy despite my groaning.
passages.sermon:
Job spoke.
Job answered.
Job said, “Today my complaint is bitter.
God’s hand feels heavy on me.
I groan, but His hand still presses me.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ גַּם־ הַ֭יּוֹם מְרִ֣י שִׂחִ֑י יָ֝דִ֗י כָּבְדָ֥ה עַל־ אַנְחָתִֽי׃

passages.text: If only I knew where to find Him, so that I could go to His seat.
passages.sermon:
Job is suffering.
Job wants to speak with God.
Job does not know where to find God.
Job wishes he could find God.
Job wants to approach God's throne.
passages.original: מִֽי־ יִתֵּ֣ן יָ֭דַעְתִּי וְאֶמְצָאֵ֑הוּ אָ֝ב֗וֹא עַד־ תְּכוּנָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: I would plead my case before Him and fill my mouth with arguments.
passages.sermon:
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
\r\nJob wants to speak to God.
\r\nJob wants to present his case to God.
\r\nJob would stand before God.
\r\nJob would explain his situation to God.
\r\nJob would speak many arguments to God.
\r\nJob would fill his mouth with reasons and explanations.
passages.original: אֶעֶרְכָ֣ה לְפָנָ֣יו מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּ֝פִ֗י אֲמַלֵּ֥א תוֹכָחֽוֹת׃

passages.text: I would learn how He would answer, and consider what He would say.
passages.sermon: Job wants to speak with God.\r\nJob wants to know how God would answer him.\r\nJob wants to understand what God would say to him.
passages.original: אֵ֭דְעָה מִלִּ֣ים יַעֲנֵ֑נִי וְ֝אָבִ֗ינָה מַה־ יֹּ֥אמַר לִֽי׃

passages.text: Would He contend with me in His great power? No, He would certainly take note of me.
passages.sermon:
God is all-powerful.
God could use His great power to argue with me.
God would not do that.
God would pay attention to me.
passages.original: הַבְּרָב־ כֹּ֭חַ יָרִ֣יב עִמָּדִ֑י לֹ֥א אַךְ־ ה֝֗וּא יָשִׂ֥ם בִּֽי׃

passages.text: Then an upright man could reason with Him, and I would be delivered forever from my Judge.
passages.sermon:
An upright man can stand before God.
This man can reason with God.
God is the Judge.
If I am upright, I can speak with God.
God will listen to my case.
God will deliver me from judgment forever.
passages.original: שָׁ֗ם יָ֭שָׁר נוֹכָ֣ח עִמּ֑וֹ וַאֲפַלְּטָ֥ה לָ֝נֶ֗צַח מִשֹּׁפְטִֽי׃

passages.text: If I go east, He is not there, and if I go west, I cannot find Him.
passages.sermon: Job speaks about God.\r\nJob says, “If I go east, I do not find God there.\r\nIf I go west, I cannot understand or find Him.”
passages.original: הֵ֤ן קֶ֣דֶם אֶהֱלֹ֣ךְ וְאֵינֶ֑נּוּ וְ֝אָח֗וֹר וְֽלֹא־ אָבִ֥ין לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When He is at work in the north, I cannot behold Him; when He turns to the south, I cannot see Him.
passages.sermon:
God is the subject.
God acts in the north.
I cannot grasp Him there.
God turns to the south.
I do not see Him there.
passages.original: שְׂמֹ֣אול בַּעֲשֹׂת֣וֹ וְלֹא־ אָ֑חַז יַעְטֹ֥ף יָ֝מִ֗ין וְלֹ֣א אֶרְאֶֽה׃

passages.text: Yet He knows the way I have taken; when He has tested me, I will come forth as gold.
passages.sermon: God knows the way I have taken.\r\nGod tests me.\r\nAfter His test, I will come forth as gold.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יָ֭דַע דֶּ֣רֶךְ עִמָּדִ֑י בְּ֝חָנַ֗נִי כַּזָּהָ֥ב אֵצֵֽא׃

passages.text: My feet have followed in His tracks; I have kept His way without turning aside.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a righteous man who suffers greatly.
Job says, "My feet have followed in God's tracks."
I have kept God's way.
I did not turn aside from His path.
passages.original: בַּ֭אֲשֻׁרוֹ אָחֲזָ֣ה רַגְלִ֑י דַּרְכּ֖וֹ שָׁמַ֣רְתִּי וְלֹא־ אָֽט׃

passages.text: I have not departed from the command of His lips; I have treasured the words of His mouth more than my daily bread.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks about his faithfulness to God.
Job says, “I have not turned away from God’s command.”
God gave commands with His own lips.
I have obeyed these commands.
I have treasured God’s words.
I value His words more than my daily food.
passages.original: מִצְוַ֣ת שְׂ֭פָתָיו וְלֹ֣א אָמִ֑ישׁ מֵ֝חֻקִּ֗י צָפַ֥נְתִּי אִמְרֵי־ פִֽיו׃

passages.text: But He is unchangeable, and who can oppose Him? He does what He desires.
passages.sermon:
God is unchangeable.
No one can oppose God.
God does what He desires.
No one can stop Him.
God acts according to His will.
God remains the same always.
passages.original: וְה֣וּא בְ֭אֶחָד וּמִ֣י יְשִׁיבֶ֑נּוּ וְנַפְשׁ֖וֹ אִוְּתָ֣ה וַיָּֽעַשׂ׃

passages.text: For He carries out His decree against me, and He has many such plans.
passages.sermon:
God acts according to His own will.
God fulfills His decree against me.
God has many similar plans.
God holds many purposes with Him.
No one can change what God decides.
God’s actions are not limited to me alone.
passages.original: כִּ֭י יַשְׁלִ֣ים חֻקִּ֑י וְכָהֵ֖נָּה רַבּ֣וֹת עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Therefore I am terrified in His presence; when I consider this, I fear Him.
passages.sermon:
God is powerful and unchangeable.
No one can oppose God.
God does what He desires.
When I stand before God, I feel terrified.
When I think about God, I fear Him.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֭ן מִפָּנָ֣יו אֶבָּהֵ֑ל אֶ֝תְבּוֹנֵ֗ן וְאֶפְחַ֥ד מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has terrified me.
passages.sermon:
God acts with great power.
God has made my heart weak.
The Almighty has filled me with fear.
God has caused my heart to tremble.
The Almighty has terrified me.

passages.text: Yet I am not silenced by the darkness, by the thick darkness that covers my face.
passages.sermon: I am not silenced by darkness.\r\nThick darkness covers my face.\r\nStill, I am not silenced.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ לֹ֣א נִ֭צְמַתִּי מִפְּנֵי־ חֹ֑שֶׁךְ וּ֝מִפָּנַ֗י כִּסָּה־ אֹֽפֶל׃
